polaroidSlides.title: Silicon Core V2
polaroidSlides.caption: Custom RP2040 breakout board soldered during 48hr hardware sprint.
polaroidSlides.details: Engineered from scratch during an intense 48-hour hardware sprint. Silicon Core V2 integrates a dual-core RP2040 MCU with custom power delivery circuitry, dedicated 16MB QSPI flash, and high-speed differential signal routing. The board serves as the fundamental computing hub for NeoGen's modular sensor payloads, running bare-metal C++ firmware with zero external operating system overhead.
polaroidSlides.specs: RP2040 Dual-Core • 133MHz • 16MB QSPI Flash • KiCad 8 4-Layer PCB • 3.3V LDO

polaroidSlides.title: Autonomous Rover
polaroidSlides.caption: LIDAR mapping and Sub-GHz telemetry testing in Delhi.
polaroidSlides.details: A ground-up cyber-physical rover designed for rugged off-road autonomous exploration and environmental mapping. Features 360-degree LiDAR simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), wheel-encoder odometry, and an ultra-reliable 433MHz Sub-GHz telemetry link delivering live kinematic data up to 3 kilometers away without Wi-Fi or cellular connectivity.
polaroidSlides.specs: ROS2 Humble • RPLiDAR A1 • STM32F4 Motion Controller • 433MHz LoRa Telemetry • 12V LiFePO4

polaroidSlides.title: LoRa Mesh Node
polaroidSlides.caption: Solar-powered environmental sensor grid running on ESP32.
polaroidSlides.details: Ultra-low power autonomous field node engineered to run indefinitely on a single 18650 lithium cell paired with a 2W solar harvester. Nodes self-organize into a resilient multi-hop mesh network over Semtech SX1262 transceivers, collecting microclimate data, soil moisture, and atmospheric particulate metrics across remote campus regions.
polaroidSlides.specs: ESP32-S3 • SX1262 LoRa 868MHz • BME680 Environmental Sensor • Deep-Sleep 15uA • 3D Printed IP67 Shell

polaroidSlides.title: Edge AI Vision
polaroidSlides.caption: Quantized neural model inference running bare-metal on ARM Cortex-M55.
polaroidSlides.details: Pioneering tiny machine learning on extreme edge microcontrollers. This project takes quantized MobileNet models (INT8 precision) and compiles them directly into ARM CMSIS-NN instructions, achieving 18 frames per second person-detection on a battery-powered camera module drawing under 120 milliwatts.
polaroidSlides.specs: ARM Cortex-M55 • Ethos-U55 NPU • TensorFlow Lite Micro • 18 FPS • 110mW Active Power

polaroidSlides.title: Maker Lab Night
polaroidSlides.caption: Late night reflow soldering, logic analyzer debugging, and firmware flashing.
polaroidSlides.details: A raw look inside our overnight hardware build sessions. Student engineers gather with hot air rework stations, USB logic analyzers, and oscilloscopes to debug I2C bus contention, trace high-frequency noise spikes, and flash bare-metal RTOS bootloaders before sunrise.
polaroidSlides.specs: Rigol DS1054Z Scope • Saleae Logic Pro • TS100 Smart Iron • Lead-Free Sn96.5 SMD Paste

polaroidSlides.title: Firmware Flash
polaroidSlides.caption: Zero-latency FreeRTOS sensor fusion testing on physical silicon.
polaroidSlides.details: Hard real-time deterministic firmware architecture written in bare-metal C. Utilizing FreeRTOS preemptive scheduling to read 6-axis IMU sensors at 1000Hz, execute Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) calculations, and output PWM motor actuation commands with under 250 microseconds of total loop jitter.
polaroidSlides.specs: FreeRTOS Kernel v10 • 1000Hz IMU Loop • Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) • SWD Debug via J-Link
